        # Start as pro
        response = requests.get(f"{BASE_URL}/private", headers={"X-API-Key": api_key})
        assert response.status_code == 200
        
        # Downgrade to free
        response = requests.post(
            f"{BASE_URL}/subscription/downgrade",
            json={"tier": "free"},
            headers={"X-API-Key": api_key}
        )
        assert response.status_code == 200
        
        # Should lose access at end of billing period
        # For testing, we might have an endpoint to simulate period end
        response = requests.post(
            f"{BASE_URL}/test/advance-billing",
            headers={"X-API-Key": api_key}
        )
        
        # Now should be blocked
        response = requests.get(f"{BASE_URL}/private", headers={"X-API-Key": api_key})
        assert response.status_code == 403
        
        # Rate limit should be free tier
        response = requests.get(f"{BASE_URL}/test", headers={"X-API-Key": api_key})
        limit = int(response.headers['X-RateLimit-Limit'])
        assert limit == 10  # Free tier limit
    
    def test_trial_period(self):
        """Test trial period functionality"""
        api_key = "test-trial-key"
        
        # Start trial
        response = requests.post(
            f"{BASE_URL}/subscription/start-trial",
            json={"tier": "pro"},
            headers={"X-API-Key": api_key}
        )
        assert response.status_code == 200
        trial_end = response.json()['trial_end']
        
        # Should have pro access during trial
        response = requests.get(f"{BASE_URL}/private", headers={"X-API-Key": api_key})
        assert response.status_code == 200
        
        # Simulate trial end
        response = requests.post(
            f"{BASE_URL}/test/advance-time",
            json={"days": 15},  # 14-day trial
            headers={"X-API-Key": api_key}
        )
        
        # Should now be blocked (unless converted)
        response = requests.get(f"{BASE_URL}/private", headers={"X-API-Key": api_key})
        assert response.status_code == 403
        
        # Should have option to convert
        data = response.json()
        assert 'convert_url' in data
    
    def test_cancellation(self):
        """Test subscription cancellation"""
        api_key = "test-cancel-key"
        
        # Cancel subscription
        response = requests.post(
            f"{BASE_URL}/subscription/cancel",
            headers={"X-API-Key": api_key}
        )
        assert response.status_code == 200
        access_until = response.json()['access_until']
        
        # Should still have access until end of period
        response = requests.get(f"{BASE_URL}/private", headers={"X-API-Key": api_key})
        assert response.status_code == 200
        
        # Simulate period end
        response = requests.post(
            f"{BASE_URL}/test/advance-billing",
            headers={"X-API-Key": api_key}
        )
        
        # Should now be blocked
        response = requests.get(f"{BASE_URL}/private", headers={"X-API-Key": api_key})
        assert response.status_code == 403
        
        # Should be able to reactivate
        response = requests.post(
            f"{BASE_URL}/subscription/reactivate",
            headers={"X-API-Key": api_key}
        )
        assert response.status_code == 200
        
        # Access restored
        response = requests.get(f"{BASE_URL}/private", headers={"X-API-Key": api_key})
        assert response.status_code == 200
    
    def test_invoice_generation(self):
        """Test invoice generation at end of billing period"""
        api_key = "test-invoice-key"
        
        # Generate usage
        for _ in range(500):
            requests.get(f"{BASE_URL}/test", headers={"X-API-Key": api_key})
        
        # Simulate end of billing period
        response = requests.post(
            f"{BASE_URL}/test/end-billing-period",
            headers={"X-API-Key": api_key}
        )

        invoices = requests.get(f"{BASE_URL}/billing/invoices", headers={"X-API-Key": api_key}).json()
        assert len(invoices) > 0
        latest = invoices[-1]
        
        assert latest['total'] > 0
        assert latest['period_end'] is not None
        assert latest['paid'] is False
        
        # Mark as paid
        response = requests.post(
            f"{BASE_URL}/billing/pay-invoice/{latest['id']}",
            headers={"X-API-Key": api_key}
        )
        assert response.status_code == 200
        
        # Check status updated
        invoice = requests.get(
            f"{BASE_URL}/billing/invoices/{latest['id']}",
            headers={"X-API-Key": api_key}
        ).json()
        assert invoice['paid'] is True

class TestBillingEdgeCases:
    def test_simultaneous_requests_at_boundary(self):
        """Test multiple requests exactly at quota boundary"""
        api_key = "test-boundary-key"
        
        # Reset quota to exactly 1 remaining
        requests.post(f"{BASE_URL}/test/set-quota", json={"remaining": 1}, headers={"X-API-Key": api_key})
        
        # Send 5 concurrent requests
        def send_request():
            return requests.get(f"{BASE_URL}/test", headers={"X-API-Key": api_key})
        
        with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=5) as executor:
            futures = [executor.submit(send_request) for _ in range(5)]
            responses = [f.result() for f in futures]
        
        # Exactly one should succeed
        successes = sum(1 for r in responses if r.status_code == 200)
        failures = sum(1 for r in responses if r.status_code == 429)
        
        assert successes == 1
        assert failures == 4
    
    def test_negative_balances(self):
        """Test handling of negative balances"""
        api_key = "test-negative-key"
        
        # Set negative balance
        requests.post(f"{BASE_URL}/billing/set-balance", json={"balance": -50.00}, headers={"X-API-Key": api_key})
        
        # Try to use API
        response = requests.get(f"{BASE_URL}/test", headers={"X-API-Key": api_key})
        
        # Should be blocked or warned
        assert response.status_code == 402  # Payment Required
        data = response.json()
        assert 'balance_due' in data
        assert data['balance_due'] == 50.00
        
        # Add payment
        requests.post(f"{BASE_URL}/billing/pay", json={"amount": 50.00}, headers={"X-API-Key": api_key})
        
        # Should work now
        response = requests.get(f"{BASE_URL}/test", headers={"X-API-Key": api_key})
        assert response.status_code == 200
    
    def test_currency_conversion(self):
        """Test multi-currency billing"""
        api_key = "test-currency-key"
        
        # Set customer currency to EUR
        requests.post(f"{BASE_URL}/account/settings", json={"currency": "EUR"}, headers={"X-API-Key": api_key})
        
        # Generate usage
        for _ in range(100):
            requests.get(f"{BASE_URL}/test", headers={"X-API-Key": api_key})
        
        # Generate invoice
        invoice = requests.post(f"{BASE_URL}/billing/generate-invoice", headers={"X-API-Key": api_key}).json()
        
        # Should be in EUR
        assert invoice['currency'] == 'EUR'
        assert invoice['total_eur'] is not None
        
        # Conversion should be reasonable
        eur_per_usd = 0.92  # Example rate
        assert abs(invoice['total_eur'] - (invoice['total_usd'] * eur_per_usd)) < 0.01
    
    def test_payment_method_expiry(self):
        """Test handling of expired payment methods"""
        api_key = "test-expiry-key"
        
        # Set payment method to expire soon
        requests.post(
            f"{BASE_URL}/billing/payment-method",
            json={"exp_month": 1, "exp_year": 2025},
            headers={"X-API-Key": api_key}
        )
        
        # Should get warning
        response = requests.get(f"{BASE_URL}/billing/payment-method", headers={"X-API-Key": api_key})
        data = response.json()
        assert data['expiring_soon'] is True
        
        # Attempt payment with expired card
        response = requests.post(f"{BASE_URL}/billing/pay", json={"amount": 10.00}, headers={"X-API-Key": api_key})
        assert response.status_code == 402
        data = response.json()
        assert data['code'] == 'PAYMENT_METHOD_EXPIRED'
    
    def test_invoice_disputes(self):
        """Test handling of invoice disputes"""
        api_key = "test-dispute-key"
        
        # Generate invoice
        invoice = requests.post(f"{BASE_URL}/billing/generate-invoice", headers={"X-API-Key": api_key}).json()
        invoice_id = invoice['id']
        
        # Mark invoice as disputed
        response = requests.post(
            f"{BASE_URL}/billing/dispute",
            json={"invoice_id": invoice_id, "reason": "fraudulent"},
            headers={"X-API-Key": api_key}
        )
        assert response.status_code == 200
        
        # Account should be frozen
        response = requests.get(f"{BASE_URL}/test", headers={"X-API-Key": api_key})
        assert response.status_code == 403
        data = response.json()
        assert data['code'] == 'ACCOUNT_FROZEN'
        
        # Resolve dispute
        response = requests.post(
            f"{BASE_URL}/billing/resolve-dispute",
            json={"invoice_id": invoice_id},
            headers={"X-API-Key": api_key}
        )
        assert response.status_code == 200
        
        # Account unfrozen
        response = requests.get(f"{BASE_URL}/test", headers={"X-API-Key": api_key})
        assert response.status_code == 200

content.value:
Monetization testing is critical for any API that generates revenue. The complexity of rate limiting, quota enforcement, usage tracking, billing, and subscription management creates numerous opportunities for bugs that can cost you money or erode customer trust.

A comprehensive test suite should cover:
- Rate limiting and quota enforcement under normal and burst conditions
- Accurate usage tracking across all request types
- Billing calculations for all pricing models
- Subscription lifecycle from trial to cancellation
- Webhook handling for payment events
- Edge cases like concurrent requests at boundaries
- Analytics dashboards for data accuracy

Automate these tests and run them regularly. When money is on the line, you can't afford to rely on manual checks. Your customers—and your bottom line—will thank you.

tutorials.title: Payment Gateway API Testing: Complete Case Study
tutorials.description: End-to-end payment API testing: idempotency, double-spending prevention, transaction rollback, concurrency, webhook testing, PCI compliance, and fraud detection.

content.value:
Payment APIs are among the most critical and complex systems in modern software. They handle real money, must be highly available, need to prevent fraud, and must maintain perfect consistency across distributed systems. A single bug can cause financial loss, regulatory violations, and catastrophic loss of customer trust.

This case study walks through testing a hypothetical payment gateway called "PayFlow." We'll cover everything from basic transaction processing to advanced scenarios like double-spending prevention, idempotency, webhook reliability, and PCI compliance.

content.title: Payment API Architecture
content.caption: Payment APIs demand the highest levels of reliability, security, and data integrity
Payment API OpenAPI Specification (Simplified)
content.code:
openapi: 3.0.3
info:
  title: PayFlow Payment API
  version: 1.0.0
  description: Payment processing API with idempotency and webhooks

components:
  schemas:
    PaymentRequest:
      type: object
      required:
        - amount
        - currency
        - paymentMethod
        - idempotencyKey
      properties:
        amount:
          type: integer
          description: Amount in smallest currency unit (cents)
          minimum: 1
          maximum: 99999999
        currency:
          type: string
          enum: [USD, EUR, GBP, JPY]
          default: USD
        paymentMethod:
          type: object
          required:
            - type
          properties:
            type:
              type: string
              enum: [card, bank, wallet]
            card:
              type: object
              properties:
                number:
                  type: string
                  pattern: '^[0-9]{16}$'
                expiryMonth:
                  type: integer
                  minimum: 1
                  maximum: 12
                expiryYear:
                  type: integer
                  minimum: 2025
                cvv:
                  type: string
                  pattern: '^[0-9]{3,4}$'
        idempotencyKey:
          type: string
          format: uuid
          description: Unique key to prevent duplicate processing
        metadata:
          type: object
          additionalProperties: true
          description: Custom metadata for the transaction

    PaymentResponse:
      type: object
      properties:
        id:
          type: string
          format: uuid
        status:
          type: string
          enum: [pending, processing, succeeded, failed, refunded]
        amount:
          type: integer
        currency:
          type: string
        createdAt:
          type: string
          format: date-time
        processedAt:
          type: string
          format: date-time
        error:
          type: object
          properties:
            code:
              type: string
            message:
              type: string

    WebhookPayload:
      type: object
      properties:
        id:
          type: string
          format: uuid
        type:
          type: string
          enum: [payment.succeeded, payment.failed, payment.refunded, payment.disputed]
        created:
          type: integer
          description: Unix timestamp
        data:
          type: object
        signature:
          type: string
          description: HMAC-SHA256 signature for verification

paths:
  /v1/payments:
    post:
      summary: Process a payment
      operationId: processPayment
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema:
              $ref: '#/components/schemas/PaymentRequest'
      responses:
        '200':
          description: Payment processing initiated
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: '#/components/schemas/PaymentResponse'
        '400':
          description: Invalid request
        '409':
          description: Duplicate idempotency key
        '402':
          description: Payment failed (insufficient funds, etc.)

  /v1/payments/{id}:
    get:
      summary: Get payment details
      parameters:
        - name: id
          in: path
          required: true
          schema:
            type: string
            format: uuid
      responses:
        '200':
          description: Payment details
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: '#/components/schemas/PaymentResponse'
        '404':
          description: Payment not found

  /v1/payments/{id}/refund:
    post:
      summary: Refund a payment
      parameters:
        - name: id
          in: path
          required: true
        - name: idempotencyKey
          in: header
          required: true
          schema:
            type: string
            format: uuid
      requestBody:
        content:
          application/json:
            schema:
              type: object
              properties:
                amount:
                  type: integer
                  description: Amount to refund (null for full refund)
      responses:
        '200':
          description: Refund processed

content.value: Idempotency is the most critical feature of any payment API. If a client retries a request due to network issues, you must not charge the customer twice. Testing idempotency ensures that duplicate requests with the same idempotency key return the same result without processing the payment again.

content.value: Double-spending occurs when the same funds are used for multiple transactions. This can happen due to race conditions, distributed system inconsistencies, or bugs in transaction handling. Testing double-spending prevention is critical for any payment system.

│  │   TRANSACTION B        WRITE B SUCCESS       READ: B ALLOWED   │ │

content.value: Payment transactions often involve multiple steps: authorization, capture, settlement, and notification. If any step fails, the entire transaction must roll back to a consistent state. Testing rollback ensures that partial failures don't leave the system in an inconsistent state.

content.caption: Transaction Rollback Tests
content.code:
class TestTransactionRollback:
    def test_full_rollback_on_failure(self):
        """Test that all steps roll back if any step fails"""
        account_id = "test-rollback-123"
        
        # Set initial balance
        requests.post(
            f"{BASE_URL}/test/set-balance",
            json={"account_id": account_id, "balance": 10000}
        )
        
        # Configure bank API to fail after authorization
        requests.post(
            f"{BASE_URL}/test/set-bank-behavior",
            json={"fail_step": "capture"}
        )
        
        # Attempt payment
        response = requests.post(
            f"{BASE_URL}/payments",
            json={
                "amount": 5000,
                "currency": "USD",
                "paymentMethod": {
                    "type": "card",
                    "card": {
                        "number": "4111111111111111",
                        "expiryMonth": 12,
                        "expiryYear": 2026,
                        "cvv": "123"
                    }
                },
                "idempotencyKey": str(uuid.uuid4())
            },
            headers={"X-API-Key": API_KEY}
        )
        
        # Should fail with specific error
        assert response.status_code == 500
        data = response.json()
        assert data['error']['code'] == 'CAPTURE_FAILED'
        
        # Verify account balance unchanged (rollback happened)
        balance = requests.get(f"{BASE_URL}/accounts/{account_id}/balance").json()
        assert balance['balance'] == 10000
        
        # Verify no transaction recorded
        transactions = requests.get(
            f"{BASE_URL}/accounts/{account_id}/transactions"
        ).json()
        assert len(transactions) == 0
    
    def test_partial_rollback_on_timeout(self):
        """Test rollback when downstream service times out"""
        account_id = "test-rollback-timeout"
        
        requests.post(f"{BASE_URL}/test/set-balance", json={"balance": 10000})
        
        # Configure timeout
        requests.post(
            f"{BASE_URL}/test/set-bank-timeout",
            json={"timeout_ms": 30000}  # Will timeout
        )
        
        start = time.time()
        response = requests.post(
            f"{BASE_URL}/payments",
            json={
                "amount": 5000,
                "paymentMethod": {...},
                "idempotencyKey": str(uuid.uuid4())
            }
        )
        duration = time.time() - start
        
        # Should timeout and rollback
        assert response.status_code == 504  # Gateway Timeout
        
        # Should have rolled back quickly (< 5s)
        assert duration < 5
        
        # Verify balance unchanged
        balance = requests.get(f"{BASE_URL}/accounts/{account_id}/balance").json()
        assert balance['balance'] == 10000
    
    def test_compensating_transactions(self):
        """Test compensating transactions for partial success"""
        account_id = "test-compensate"
        
        # Scenario: Bank authorized but settlement failed
        # Should issue compensating transaction (void authorization)
        
        requests.post(f"{BASE_URL}/test/set-balance", json={"balance": 10000})
        
        # Configure: authorize succeeds, settlement fails
        requests.post(
            f"{BASE_URL}/test/set-bank-behavior",
            json={"fail_step": "settlement"}
        )
        
        response = requests.post(
            f"{BASE_URL}/payments",
            json={
                "amount": 5000,
                "paymentMethod": {...},
                "idempotencyKey": str(uuid.uuid4())
            }
        )
        
        assert response.status_code == 500
        
        # Verify compensating transaction was issued
        audit = requests.get(f"{BASE_URL}/audit").json()
        
        # Should have authorize + void
        authorize = [e for e in audit if e['type'] == 'authorization']
        void = [e for e in audit if e['type'] == 'void']
        
        assert len(authorize) == 1
        assert len(void) == 1
        assert void[0]['authorization_id'] == authorize[0]['id']

    def test_webhook_signature_verification(self):

        # Get last webhook from audit log
        webhook = requests.get(f"{BASE_URL}/webhooks/last").json()
        
        # Verify signature
        payload = webhook['payload']
        signature = webhook['signature']
        
        # Recreate signature
        expected_signature = hmac.new(
            key=secret.encode(),
            msg=json.dumps(payload, sort_keys=True).encode(),
            digestmod=hashlib.sha256
        ).hexdigest()
        
        assert signature == expected_signature
        
        # Test with wrong secret
        wrong_secret = hmac.new(
            key=b'wrong',
            msg=json.dumps(payload).encode(),

    def test_webhook_idempotency(self):

        )

                "idempotencyKey": str(uuid.uuid4())
            },
            headers={"X-API-Key": API_KEY}
        )
        
        # Get audit logs
        logs = requests.get(f"{BASE_URL}/audit/logs").json()
        
        # Check that full PAN never appears
        for log in logs:
            log_str = json.dumps(log)
            assert "4111111111111111" not in log_str
            # Should be masked (e.g., "************1111")
            assert "************1111" in log_str or "xxxx-1111" in log_str
    
    def test_cvv_not_stored(self):
        """Test that CVV is never stored (PCI requirement)"""
        # Make payment
        response = requests.post(f"{BASE_URL}/payments", json={
            "amount": 1000,
            "paymentMethod": {
                "type": "card",
                "card": {
                    "number": "4111111111111111",
                    "expiryMonth": 12,
                    "expiryYear": 2026,
                    "cvv": "999"  # Test CVV
                }
            }
        })
        
        payment_id = response.json()['id']
        
        # Check database directly (requires DB access)
        payment_record = db.query(
            "SELECT * FROM payments WHERE id = %s", payment_id
        )
        
        # CVV should not be in any column
        assert 'cvv' not in payment_record
        assert '999' not in str(payment_record)
        
        # Check logs
        logs = requests.get(f"{BASE_URL}/audit/logs").json()
        for log in logs:
            log_str = json.dumps(log)
            assert '999' not in log_str
    
    def test_encryption_at_rest(self):
        """Test that sensitive data is encrypted at rest"""
        # This test requires direct DB access
        payment_id = make_test_payment()
        
        # Get raw database record
        record = db.query_raw("SELECT * FROM payments WHERE id = %s", payment_id)
        
        # Card number should be encrypted, not plaintext
        card_number_field = record['card_number']
        
        # Should be binary data, not starting with 4 (Visa prefix)
        assert isinstance(card_number_field, bytes)
        assert not card_number_field.startswith(b'4')
        
        # Decrypt and verify
        decrypted = decrypt_aes256(card_number_field, ENCRYPTION_KEY)
        assert decrypted == '4111111111111111'
    
    def test_tls_required(self):
        """Test that all endpoints require TLS 1.2+"""
        # Try HTTP (should redirect or fail)
        try:
            response = requests.get("http://api.payflow.example/health")
            assert response.status_code == 301 or response.status_code == 308
        except requests.exceptions.SSLError:
            # Connection refused for HTTP is also acceptable
            pass
        
        # HTTPS should work
        response = requests.get("https://api.payflow.example/health")
        assert response.status_code == 200
        
        # Check TLS version (requires lower-level inspection)
        import ssl
        context = ssl.create_default_context()
        with socket.create_connection(('api.payflow.example', 443)) as sock:
            with context.wrap_socket(sock, server_hostname='api.payflow.example') as ssock:
                tls_version = ssock.version()
                assert tls_version in ['TLSv1.2', 'TLSv1.3']
    
    def test_audit_logs_complete(self):
        """Test that all access to cardholder data is logged"""
        # Access payment data through API
        response = requests.get(
            f"{BASE_URL}/payments/{payment_id}",
            headers={"X-API-Key": API_KEY}
        )
        
        # Check audit logs
        logs = requests.get(f"{BASE_URL}/audit/logs").json()
        
        # Should have log entry for this access
        relevant_logs = [
            log for log in logs
            if log['resource'] == 'payment'
            and log['resource_id'] == payment_id
            and log['action'] == 'read'
        ]
        
        assert len(relevant_logs) == 1
        log = relevant_logs[0]
        assert log['user'] is not None
        assert log['timestamp'] is not None
        assert log['ip_address'] is not None
    
    def test_least_privilege_access(self):
        """Test that API keys have least privilege"""
        # Create read-only key
        key_response = requests.post(
            f"{BASE_URL}/api-keys",
            json={"permissions": ["read"]}
        )
        read_only_key = key_response.json()['key']
        
        # Try to create payment with read-only key
        response = requests.post(
            f"{BASE_URL}/payments",
            json={"amount": 1000, ...},
            headers={"X-API-Key": read_only_key}
        )
        assert response.status_code == 403
        
        # Should be able to read
        response = requests.get(
            f"{BASE_URL}/payments/{payment_id}",
            headers={"X-API-Key": read_only_key}
        )
        assert response.status_code == 200

content.title: Payment API Test Coverage Matrix
content.caption: Comprehensive test coverage ensures payment APIs are reliable, secure, and compliant

content.value:
Testing payment APIs has taught us several critical lessons:

1. **Idempotency is non-negotiable**: Without it, network retries will cause double-charging. Test concurrent duplicates, key expiry, and failed payments.

2. **Race conditions are the enemy**: Payment systems must handle concurrent operations on the same account. Use database transactions with appropriate isolation levels.

3. **Rollbacks must be complete**: Partial failures can leave systems inconsistent. Test every failure path and verify compensating transactions.

4. **Webhooks need durability**: Webhooks should survive service restarts. Test queue persistence and retry logic.

5. **PCI compliance is testable**: Don't assume you're compliant—test PAN masking, encryption, and access controls.

6. **Fraud detection needs real-world simulation**: Use historical data to validate fraud rules.

7. **Performance under load matters**: Payment APIs must handle peak loads (Black Friday, etc.). Test at 10x expected traffic.

tutorials.title: E-commerce API Testing: A Complete Case Study
tutorials.description: A comprehensive guide to testing a modern e-commerce platform. Covers product catalog, inventory management, shopping cart, order processing, payment integration, and recommendation engines with realistic testing scenarios and code examples.

content.value:
E-commerce platforms are the backbone of modern retail, handling millions of users, products, and transactions daily. Unlike simple CRUD applications, e-commerce systems are distributed, stateful, and must maintain perfect consistency between inventory, carts, and orders. A single bug can lead to overselling products, incorrect pricing, failed checkouts, or a poor user experience.

This case study walks through testing a hypothetical e-commerce platform called "ShopFast." We'll cover core functionalities, from browsing the product catalog to completing an order, and explore advanced scenarios like inventory race conditions, abandoned cart recovery, and personalized recommendation accuracy.

openapi: 3.0.3
info:
  title: ShopFast E-commerce API
  version: 1.0.0
  description: API for product catalog, cart, and order management

components:
  schemas:
    Product:
      type: object
      properties:
        id:
          type: string
          format: uuid
        sku:
          type: string
        name:
          type: string
        description:
          type: string
        price:
          type: number
          format: float
        currency:
          type: string
          enum: [USD, EUR, GBP]
        categories:
          type: array
          items:
            type: string
        attributes:
          type: object
          additionalProperties: true
        inventory:
          type: object
          properties:
            available:
              type: integer
            reserved:
              type: integer
            location:
              type: string

    CartItem:
      type: object
      required:
        - productId
        - quantity
      properties:
        productId:
          type: string
          format: uuid
        quantity:
          type: integer
          minimum: 1
          maximum: 99
        price:
          type: number
          description: Price at the time of addition

    Cart:
      type: object
      properties:
        id:
          type: string
          format: uuid
        userId:
          type: string
          format: uuid
        items:
          type: array
          items:
            $ref: '#/components/schemas/CartItem'
        subtotal:
          type: number
        createdAt:
          type: string
          format: date-time
        updatedAt:
          type: string
          format: date-time

    Order:
      type: object
      properties:
        id:
          type: string
          format: uuid
        userId:
          type: string
          format: uuid
        items:
          type: array
          items:
            $ref: '#/components/schemas/CartItem'
        total:
          type: number
        status:
          type: string
          enum: [pending, paid, shipped, delivered, cancelled]
        shippingAddress:
          type: object
        paymentId:
          type: string
        createdAt:
          type: string
          format: date-time

paths:
  /v1/products:
    get:
      summary: List products with filtering
      parameters:
        - name: category
          in: query
          schema:
            type: string
        - name: minPrice
          in: query
          schema:
            type: number
        - name: maxPrice
          in: query
          schema:
            type: number
        - name: sort
          in: query
          schema:
            type: string
            enum: [price_asc, price_desc, name]
        - name: page
          in: query
          schema:
            type: integer
            default: 1
        - name: limit
          in: query
          schema:
            type: integer
            default: 20
      responses:
        '200':
          description: List of products
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                type: object
                properties:
                  data:
                    type: array
                    items:
                      $ref: '#/components/schemas/Product'
                  total:
                    type: integer
                  page:
                    type: integer

  /v1/cart/{userId}:
    get:
      summary: Get user's cart
      parameters:
        - name: userId
          in: path
          required: true
          schema:
            type: string
            format: uuid
      responses:
        '200':
          description: Cart contents
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: '#/components/schemas/Cart'

    post:
      summary: Add item to cart
      parameters:
        - name: userId
          in: path
          required: true
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema:
              $ref: '#/components/schemas/CartItem'
      responses:
        '200':
          description: Item added
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: '#/components/schemas/Cart'
        '409':
          description: Insufficient inventory

  /v1/orders:
    post:
      summary: Create order from cart
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema:
              type: object
              required:
                - userId
                - shippingAddress
                - paymentMethod
              properties:
                userId:
                  type: string
                  format: uuid
                shippingAddress:
                  type: object
                paymentMethod:
                  type: object
                idempotencyKey:
                  type: string
                  format: uuid
      responses:
        '201':
          description: Order created
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: '#/components/schemas/Order'
        '409':
          description: Inventory conflict

content.value: The product catalog is the storefront of your API. It must handle high read loads, complex filtering, and dynamic data like pricing and availability. Testing the catalog ensures users can find products quickly and accurately.

import pytest
import requests
from urllib.parse import urlencode

class TestProductCatalog:
    BASE_URL = "https://api.shopfast.example/v1"
    API_KEY = "test-key-123"

    def test_list_products_pagination(self):
        """Test that pagination works correctly"""
        # Request first page
        response = requests.get(
            f"{self.BASE_URL}/products",
            params={"page": 1, "limit": 5},
            headers={"X-API-Key": self.API_KEY}
        )
        assert response.status_code == 200
        data = response.json()
        assert len(data['data']) <= 5
        assert data['page'] == 1
        first_page_ids = [p['id'] for p in data['data']]

        # Request second page
        response = requests.get(
            f"{self.BASE_URL}/products",
            params={"page": 2, "limit": 5},
            headers={"X-API-Key": self.API_KEY}
        )
        data = response.json()
        second_page_ids = [p['id'] for p in data['data']]

        # Ensure no overlap
        assert set(first_page_ids).isdisjoint(set(second_page_ids))

    def test_filter_by_category_and_price(self):
        """Test combined filtering by category and price range"""
        params = {
            "category": "electronics",
            "minPrice": 100.00,
            "maxPrice": 500.00,
            "sort": "price_asc"
        }
        response = requests.get(
            f"{self.BASE_URL}/products?{urlencode(params)}",
            headers={"X-API-Key": self.API_KEY}
        )
        assert response.status_code == 200
        products = response.json()['data']

        # Verify all products match criteria
        for product in products:
            assert "electronics" in product['categories']
            assert 100.00 <= product['price'] <= 500.00

        # Verify sorting
        prices = [p['price'] for p in products]
        assert prices == sorted(prices)

    def test_product_details_cache(self):
        """Test that product details are cached for performance"""
        product_id = "prod-123"

        # First request (cold cache)
        import time
        start = time.time()
        response1 = requests.get(
            f"{self.BASE_URL}/products/{product_id}",
            headers={"X-API-Key": self.API_KEY}
        )
        first_duration = time.time() - start
        assert response1.status_code == 200

        # Second request (warm cache)
        start = time.time()
        response2 = requests.get(
            f"{self.BASE_URL}/products/{product_id}",
            headers={"X-API-Key": self.API_KEY}
        )
        second_duration = time.time() - start
        assert response2.status_code == 200

        # Cached response should be significantly faster
        assert second_duration < first_duration / 2

    def test_product_search(self):
        """Test full-text search functionality"""
        search_term = "wireless headphones"
        response = requests.get(
            f"{self.BASE_URL}/products/search",
            params={"q": search_term},
            headers={"X-API-Key": self.API_KEY}
        )
        assert response.status_code == 200
        products = response.json()['data']

        # Basic relevance check: search term should appear in name or description
        for product in products:
            combined_text = f"{product['name']} {product.get('description', '')}".lower()
            assert any(word in combined_text for word in search_term.lower().split())

class TestInventoryManagement:

    def test_concurrent_reservations_last_item(self):
        """Test that two users cannot reserve the last item simultaneously"""
        product_id = "prod-last-item"
        
        # Set inventory to 1
        requests.post(
            f"{BASE_URL}/test/set-inventory",
            json={"product_id": product_id, "available": 1}
        )

        def add_to_cart(user_id):
            return requests.post(
                f"{BASE_URL}/cart/{user_id}",
                json={"productId": product_id, "quantity": 1},
                headers={"X-API-Key": API_KEY}
            )

        # Simulate two users adding to cart concurrently
        from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
        with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=2) as executor:
            futures = [
                executor.submit(add_to_cart, "user-a"),
                executor.submit(add_to_cart, "user-b")
            ]
            responses = [f.result() for f in futures]

        # One should succeed, one should fail with 409 Conflict
        status_codes = [r.status_code for r in responses]
        assert 200 in status_codes
        assert 409 in status_codes

        # Verify final inventory is 0
        product = requests.get(f"{BASE_URL}/products/{product_id}").json()
        assert product['inventory']['available'] == 0

    def test_reservation_expiry(self):
        """Test that reserved stock returns after cart timeout"""
        product_id = "prod-timeout"
        user_id = "user-timeout"
        
        # Set inventory
        requests.post(f"{BASE_URL}/test/set-inventory", json={"available": 5})
        
        # Add to cart
        response = requests.post(
            f"{BASE_URL}/cart/{user_id}",
            json={"productId": product_id, "quantity": 2}
        )
        assert response.status_code == 200
        
        # Verify inventory reduced (reserved)
        product = requests.get(f"{BASE_URL}/products/{product_id}").json()
        assert product['inventory']['available'] == 3
        
        # Simulate cart timeout (test endpoint to expire cart)
        requests.post(
            f"{BASE_URL}/test/expire-cart",
            json={"user_id": user_id}
        )
        
        # Verify inventory restored
        product = requests.get(f"{BASE_URL}/products/{product_id}").json()
        assert product['inventory']['available'] == 5

    def test_inventory_during_checkout(self):
        """Test that inventory is correctly decremented only after successful payment"""
        product_id = "prod-checkout"
        user_id = "user-checkout"
        
        # Setup
        requests.post(f"{BASE_URL}/test/set-inventory", json={"available": 3})
        
        # Add to cart
        requests.post(f"{BASE_URL}/cart/{user_id}", json={"productId": product_id, "quantity": 1})
        
        # Get cart
        cart = requests.get(f"{BASE_URL}/cart/{user_id}").json()
        
        # Attempt checkout with a failing payment
        order_data = {
            "userId": user_id,
            "shippingAddress": {},
            "paymentMethod": {"type": "card", "fail": True},  # Test flag to fail payment
            "idempotencyKey": str(uuid.uuid4())
        }
        response = requests.post(f"{BASE_URL}/orders", json=order_data)
        assert response.status_code == 402  # Payment failed
        
        # Inventory should not have changed (still reserved in cart, not sold)
        product = requests.get(f"{BASE_URL}/products/{product_id}").json()
        assert product['inventory']['available'] == 2
        
        # Now checkout with success
        order_data['paymentMethod'] = {"type": "card"}  # Succeed this time
        order_data['idempotencyKey'] = str(uuid.uuid4())
        response = requests.post(f"{BASE_URL}/orders", json=order_data)
        assert response.status_code == 201
        
        # Inventory should now be decremented
        product = requests.get(f"{BASE_URL}/products/{product_id}").json()
        assert product['inventory']['available'] == 2  # 3 - 1 (sold, not reserved)

content.value: The shopping cart is a stateful session that must persist across user sessions and devices. It must handle concurrent modifications, price changes, and item unavailability gracefully.

content.caption: Shopping Cart Tests
content.code:
class TestShoppingCart:

    def test_cart_persistence(self):
        """Test that cart persists across sessions"""
        user_id = "user-persist"
        product_id = "prod-persist"
        
        # Add item
        requests.post(f"{BASE_URL}/cart/{user_id}", json={"productId": product_id, "quantity": 2})
        
        # Simulate new session (new client, no session cookie)
        response = requests.get(f"{BASE_URL}/cart/{user_id}")
        cart = response.json()
        
        assert len(cart['items']) == 1
        assert cart['items'][0]['productId'] == product_id
        assert cart['items'][0]['quantity'] == 2

    def test_cart_concurrent_modification(self):
        """Test that concurrent updates to the same cart are handled correctly"""
        user_id = "user-concurrent"
        product_a = "prod-a"
        product_b = "prod-b"
        
        def add_item(product):
            return requests.post(
                f"{BASE_URL}/cart/{user_id}",
                json={"productId": product, "quantity": 1}
            )
        
        # Add two different items concurrently
        with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=2) as executor:
            futures = [
                executor.submit(add_item, product_a),
                executor.submit(add_item, product_b)
            ]
            responses = [f.result() for f in futures]
        
        # Both should succeed
        for r in responses:
            assert r.status_code == 200
        
        # Final cart should have both items
        cart = requests.get(f"{BASE_URL}/cart/{user_id}").json()
        assert len(cart['items']) == 2
        product_ids = [item['productId'] for item in cart['items']]
        assert product_a in product_ids
        assert product_b in product_ids

    def test_price_snapshot(self):
        """Test that cart captures price at time of addition, not current price"""
        user_id = "user-price"
        product_id = "prod-price"
        
        # Get current product price
        product = requests.get(f"{BASE_URL}/products/{product_id}").json()
        original_price = product['price']
        
        # Add to cart
        response = requests.post(f"{BASE_URL}/cart/{user_id}", json={"productId": product_id, "quantity": 1})
        cart = response.json()
        assert cart['items'][0]['price'] == original_price
        
        # Admin updates price
        requests.put(f"{BASE_URL}/admin/products/{product_id}", json={"price": original_price * 2})
        
        # Cart should still have old price
        cart = requests.get(f"{BASE_URL}/cart/{user_id}").json()
        assert cart['items'][0]['price'] == original_price
        
        # Subtotal should reflect the old price
        assert cart['subtotal'] == original_price

    def test_remove_unavailable_items(self):
        """Test that items which become unavailable are flagged or removed from cart"""
        user_id = "user-unavailable"
        product_id = "prod-unavailable"
        
        # Add item
        requests.post(f"{BASE_URL}/cart/{user_id}", json={"productId": product_id, "quantity": 1})
        
        # Make product unavailable (delete or set inventory to 0)
        requests.delete(f"{BASE_URL}/admin/products/{product_id}")
        
        # Get cart - should flag item
        cart = requests.get(f"{BASE_URL}/cart/{user_id}").json()
        item = cart['items'][0]
        assert item.get('unavailable') is True
        
        # Attempt checkout should fail or warn
        order_data = {
            "userId": user_id,
            "shippingAddress": {},
            "paymentMethod": {"type": "card"},
            "idempotencyKey": str(uuid.uuid4())
        }
        response = requests.post(f"{BASE_URL}/orders", json=order_data)
        assert response.status_code == 409
        assert response.json()['error']['code'] == 'UNAVAILABLE_PRODUCTS'

content.value: Order processing is the most critical path. It involves checking inventory, processing payment, creating an order, and sending confirmations. This must be atomic and idempotent to prevent issues like double-charging or overselling.

content.caption: Order Processing Tests
content.code:
class TestOrderProcessing:

    def test_checkout_idempotency(self):
        """Test that duplicate checkout requests don't create duplicate orders"""
        user_id = "user-order-idem"
        product_id = "prod-order-idem"
        idempotency_key = str(uuid.uuid4())
        
        # Setup: add item to cart
        requests.post(f"{BASE_URL}/cart/{user_id}", json={"productId": product_id, "quantity": 1})
        
        order_data = {
            "userId": user_id,
            "shippingAddress": {"line1": "123 Main St"},
            "paymentMethod": {"type": "card"},
            "idempotencyKey": idempotency_key
        }
        
        # First request
        response1 = requests.post(f"{BASE_URL}/orders", json=order_data)
        assert response1.status_code == 201
        order_id = response1.json()['id']
        
        # Duplicate request with same key
        response2 = requests.post(f"{BASE_URL}/orders", json=order_data)
        assert response2.status_code == 200  # Returns existing order, not 201
        assert response2.json()['id'] == order_id
        
        # Verify only one order exists
        user_orders = requests.get(f"{BASE_URL}/users/{user_id}/orders").json()
        assert len(user_orders) == 1

    def test_checkout_atomicity(self):
        """Test that checkout either fully succeeds or fully fails"""
        user_id = "user-atomic"
        product_id = "prod-atomic"
        
        # Setup
        requests.post(f"{BASE_URL}/test/set-inventory", json={"available": 1})
        requests.post(f"{BASE_URL}/cart/{user_id}", json={"productId": product_id, "quantity": 1})
        
        # Configure payment to fail after inventory check
        requests.post(f"{BASE_URL}/test/set-payment-behavior", json={"fail_after": "inventory_check"})
        
        order_data = {
            "userId": user_id,
            "shippingAddress": {},
            "paymentMethod": {"type": "card"},
            "idempotencyKey": str(uuid.uuid4())
        }
        
        # Attempt order
        response = requests.post(f"{BASE_URL}/orders", json=order_data)
        assert response.status_code == 402  # Payment failed
        
        # Verify inventory is back to original state (not sold, not reserved)
        product = requests.get(f"{BASE_URL}/products/{product_id}").json()
        assert product['inventory']['available'] == 1
        
        # Verify no order was created
        user_orders = requests.get(f"{BASE_URL}/users/{user_id}/orders").json()
        assert len(user_orders) == 0

    def test_order_state_transitions(self):
        """Test that orders move through valid states"""
        user_id = "user-state"
        
        # Create order
        order_data = {
            "userId": user_id,
            "shippingAddress": {},
            "paymentMethod": {"type": "card"},
            "idempotencyKey": str(uuid.uuid4())
        }
        response = requests.post(f"{BASE_URL}/orders", json=order_data)
        order_id = response.json()['id']
        assert response.json()['status'] == 'pending'
        
        # Simulate payment webhook
        requests.post(f"{BASE_URL}/webhooks/payment", json={"orderId": order_id, "status": "succeeded"})
        
        # Check status
        order = requests.get(f"{BASE_URL}/orders/{order_id}").json()
        assert order['status'] == 'paid'
        
        # Ship order
        requests.post(f"{BASE_URL}/admin/orders/{order_id}/ship")
        order = requests.get(f"{BASE_URL}/orders/{order_id}").json()
        assert order['status'] == 'shipped'
        
        # Try invalid transition (shipped -> cancelled)
        response = requests.post(f"{BASE_URL}/admin/orders/{order_id}/cancel")
        assert response.status_code == 409  # Conflict, invalid state transition

    def test_large_order_validation(self):
        """Test that orders with large quantities are handled correctly"""
        user_id = "user-large"
        product_id = "prod-large"
        
        # Set inventory to 100
        requests.post(f"{BASE_URL}/test/set-inventory", json={"available": 100})
        
        # Add 50 items to cart (valid)
        response = requests.post(f"{BASE_URL}/cart/{user_id}", json={"productId": product_id, "quantity": 50})
        assert response.status_code == 200
        
        # Try to add 60 more (total 110 > 100)
        response = requests.post(f"{BASE_URL}/cart/{user_id}", json={"productId": product_id, "quantity": 60})
        assert response.status_code == 409
        data = response.json()
        assert data['error']['code'] == 'INSUFFICIENT_INVENTORY'
        
        # Checkout should succeed with 50 items
        order_data = {"userId": user_id, "shippingAddress": {}, "paymentMethod": {"type": "card"}}
        response = requests.post(f"{BASE_URL}/orders", json=order_data)
        assert response.status_code == 201
        assert response.json()['total'] == 50 * get_product_price(product_id)

content.value: Recommendation engines drive sales by showing users relevant products. Testing them is different from functional testing—it's about relevance, diversity, and performance. You need to ensure the algorithms are working as expected and not creating filter bubbles or showing inappropriate items.

content.caption: Recommendation Engine Tests
content.code:
class TestRecommendationEngine:

    def test_personalization(self):
        """Test that different users get different recommendations"""
        # User A with browsing history in electronics
        requests.post(f"{BASE_URL}/test/set-history", json={
            "user": "user-a",
            "views": ["laptop", "phone", "headphones"]
        })
        
        # User B with history in clothing
        requests.post(f"{BASE_URL}/test/set-history", json={
            "user": "user-b",
            "views": ["shirt", "pants", "shoes"]
        })
        
        # Get recommendations
        recs_a = requests.get(f"{BASE_URL}/users/user-a/recommendations").json()
        recs_b = requests.get(f"{BASE_URL}/users/user-b/recommendations").json()
        
        # They should be different
        assert recs_a != recs_b
        
        # Verify categories match history
        recs_a_cats = [p['categories'] for p in recs_a]
        recs_b_cats = [p['categories'] for p in recs_b]
        assert any("electronics" in cats for cats in recs_a_cats)
        assert any("clothing" in cats for cats in recs_b_cats)

    def test_recommendation_diversity(self):
        """Test that recommendations are not all from the same category"""
        user_id = "user-diversity"
        
        # Set history in one category
        requests.post(f"{BASE_URL}/test/set-history", json={
            "user": user_id,
            "views": ["laptop"]
        })
        
        recs = requests.get(f"{BASE_URL}/users/{user_id}/recommendations", params={"limit": 10}).json()
        
        # Should have some diversity (not all laptops)
        categories = set()
        for product in recs:
            categories.update(product['categories'])
        
        assert len(categories) > 1

    def test_real_time_personalization(self):
        """Test that recommendations update after user actions"""
        user_id = "user-realtime"
        
        # Get recommendations for new user
        initial_recs = requests.get(f"{BASE_URL}/users/{user_id}/recommendations").json()
        
        # User views a specific product
        requests.post(f"{BASE_URL}/events", json={
            "user": user_id,
            "type": "product_view",
            "product": "gaming-chair"
        })
        
        # Get new recommendations
        new_recs = requests.get(f"{BASE_URL}/users/{user_id}/recommendations").json()
        
        # Should be different
        assert initial_recs != new_recs
        
        # Should now include gaming-related items
        gaming_related = [p for p in new_recs if 'gaming' in p['name'].lower() or 'gaming' in p['categories']]
        assert len(gaming_related) > 0

    def test_recommendation_latency(self):
        """Test that recommendations are fast enough for real-time use"""
        user_id = "user-latency"
        
        import time
        start = time.time()
        response = requests.get(f"{BASE_URL}/users/{user_id}/recommendations")
        duration = time.time() - start
        
        assert response.status_code == 200
        assert duration < 0.2  # 200ms SLA for recommendations

    def test_fallback_strategy(self):
        """Test fallback when user has no history"""
        user_id = "user-fallback"
        
        # No history for this user
        recs = requests.get(f"{BASE_URL}/users/{user_id}/recommendations").json()
        
        # Should return popular items
        assert len(recs) > 0
        
        # Should be different from personalized recs of another user
        other_user_recs = requests.get(f"{BASE_URL}/users/user-with-history/recommendations").json()
        assert recs != other_user_recs

content.title: E-commerce Test Coverage Matrix
content.caption: Comprehensive test coverage ensures e-commerce reliability and a smooth user experience

content.value:
Testing e-commerce APIs has taught us several critical lessons:

1. **Inventory is a hotbed for race conditions**: Always test concurrent access to the last item. Use atomic database operations and optimistic locking.

2. **Carts are stateful and need snapshots**: Prices change. Always store the price in the cart at the time of addition to avoid surprises at checkout.

3. **Idempotency saves orders**: Without idempotency keys, users clicking 'Place Order' twice will create two orders. Test this aggressively.

4. **Checkout must be atomic**: If payment fails, inventory must not be deducted. If inventory is unavailable, payment must not be processed. Test all failure paths.

5. **Recommendations are about relevance, not just correctness**: Test that recommendations are personalized, diverse, and fast. A slow or irrelevant recommendation engine is worse than none.

6. **Caching is essential but challenging**: The catalog must handle high read loads. Test cache invalidation when product data changes.

7. **User expectations are high**: E-commerce users expect a seamless experience. Test edge cases like cart timeouts, session resumption across devices, and graceful degradation when services are down.

tutorials.description: A comprehensive guide to testing a modern social media platform. Covers user authentication, posts, comments, likes, feed generation, notifications, real-time updates, content moderation, and privacy controls with realistic testing scenarios and code examples.

content.value:
Social media APIs are among the most demanding systems to build and test. They combine real-time interactions, complex data relationships, privacy concerns, and massive scale. A single user can generate hundreds of interactions per day, and the system must deliver content to millions of users with low latency.

This case study walks through testing a hypothetical social media platform called "ConnectHub." We'll cover everything from user authentication to feed generation, notifications, and real-time updates. We'll explore critical challenges like fan-out problems, timeline consistency, and content moderation at scale.

content.value: Authentication is the foundation of any social platform. Users must be able to securely sign up, log in, and manage their sessions. Authorization ensures users can only access what they're allowed to see and do.

content.caption: Authentication and Authorization Tests
content.code:
import pytest
import requests
import jwt
import time
from datetime import datetime, timedelta

class TestAuth:
    BASE_URL = "https://api.connecthub.example/v1"
    
    def test_user_registration_and_login(self):
        """Test complete user registration and login flow"""
        # Register new user
        user_data = {
            "username": f"testuser_{int(time.time())}",
            "email": f"test_{int(time.time())}@example.com",
            "password": "SecurePass123!",
            "displayName": "Test User"
        }
        
        response = requests.post(f"{self.BASE_URL}/auth/register", json=user_data)
        assert response.status_code == 201
        user = response.json()
        assert user['username'] == user_data['username']
        
        # Login with credentials
        login_data = {
            "username": user_data['username'],
            "password": user_data['password']
        }
        response = requests.post(f"{self.BASE_URL}/auth/login", json=login_data)
        assert response.status_code == 200
        tokens = response.json()
        assert 'accessToken' in tokens
        assert 'refreshToken' in tokens
        
        # Verify token works
        headers = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {tokens['accessToken']}"}
        response = requests.get(f"{self.BASE_URL}/users/me", headers=headers)
        assert response.status_code == 200
        assert response.json()['username'] == user_data['username']

    def test_token_refresh(self):
        """Test that refresh tokens can obtain new access tokens"""
        # Login to get tokens
        login_data = {"username": "existinguser", "password": "password123"}
        response = requests.post(f"{self.BASE_URL}/auth/login", json=login_data)
        tokens = response.json()
        
        # Wait a bit
        time.sleep(1)
        
        # Refresh token
        refresh_data = {"refreshToken": tokens['refreshToken']}
        response = requests.post(f"{self.BASE_URL}/auth/refresh", json=refresh_data)
        assert response.status_code == 200
        new_tokens = response.json()
        
        # New tokens should be different
        assert new_tokens['accessToken'] != tokens['accessToken']
        
        # Old token should still work until expiry
        headers = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {tokens['accessToken']}"}
        response = requests.get(f"{self.BASE_URL}/users/me", headers=headers)
        assert response.status_code == 200

    def test_authorization_scopes(self):
        """Test that tokens respect authorization scopes"""
        # Create token with read-only scope
        auth_response = requests.post(f"{self.BASE_URL}/auth/token", json={
            "username": "testuser",
            "password": "password123",
            "scope": "read"
        })
        read_token = auth_response.json()['accessToken']
        
        # Try to create a post (should fail)
        headers = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {read_token}"}
        response = requests.post(f"{self.BASE_URL}/posts", headers=headers, json={
            "content": "This should not work"
        })
        assert response.status_code == 403
        
        # Try to read (should work)
        response = requests.get(f"{self.BASE_URL}/feed/me", headers=headers)
        assert response.status_code == 200

    def test_password_reset_flow(self):
        """Test complete password reset flow"""
        # Request password reset
        response = requests.post(f"{self.BASE_URL}/auth/reset-password", json={
            "email": "user@example.com"
        })
        assert response.status_code == 200
        
        # Get reset token from test endpoint (in production this would be emailed)
        token_response = requests.get(f"{self.BASE_URL}/test/last-reset-token")
        reset_token = token_response.json()['token']
        
        # Reset password
        response = requests.post(f"{self.BASE_URL}/auth/confirm-reset", json={
            "token": reset_token,
            "newPassword": "NewSecurePass456!"
        })
        assert response.status_code == 200
        
        # Login with new password
        login_data = {"username": "user@example.com", "password": "NewSecurePass456!"}
        response = requests.post(f"{self.BASE_URL}/auth/login", json=login_data)
        assert response.status_code == 200

    def test_rate_limiting_on_auth(self):
        """Test that auth endpoints are rate limited"""
        # Attempt multiple failed logins
        for i in range(6):
            response = requests.post(f"{self.BASE_URL}/auth/login", json={
                "username": "testuser",
                "password": "wrongpassword"
            })
            if i < 5:
                assert response.status_code == 401  # Unauthorized
            else:
                assert response.status_code == 429  # Too Many Requests

class TestPostsAndInteractions:
    
    def test_create_post_with_media(self):
        """Test creating a post with text and media attachments"""
        headers = get_auth_headers("testuser")
        
        post_data = {
            "content": "Check out this amazing view! 🌅",
            "media": [
                {"type": "image", "url": "https://cdn.example.com/photo1.jpg"},
                {"type": "image", "url": "https://cdn.example.com/photo2.jpg"}
            ],
            "visibility": "public"
        }
        
        response = requests.post(f"{BASE_URL}/posts", headers=headers, json=post_data)
        assert response.status_code == 201
        post = response.json()
        assert post['content'] == post_data['content']
        assert len(post['media']) == 2
        assert post['likesCount'] == 0
        assert post['commentsCount'] == 0
        
        # Verify post appears in user's profile
        response = requests.get(f"{BASE_URL}/users/testuser/posts", headers=headers)
        posts = response.json()
        assert any(p['id'] == post['id'] for p in posts)

    def test_like_unlike_post(self):
        """Test liking and unliking a post (idempotent)"""
        headers = get_auth_headers("testuser")
        
        # Create a post
        post_response = requests.post(f"{BASE_URL}/posts", headers=headers, json={
            "content": "Post for like testing"
        })
        post_id = post_response.json()['id']
        
        # Like the post
        like_response = requests.post(f"{BASE_URL}/posts/{post_id}/like", headers=headers)
        assert like_response.status_code == 200
        
        # Get post and verify like count
        post = requests.get(f"{BASE_URL}/posts/{post_id}").json()
        assert post['likesCount'] == 1
        
        # Try to like again (should be idempotent)
        like_response2 = requests.post(f"{BASE_URL}/posts/{post_id}/like", headers=headers)
        assert like_response2.status_code == 200  # Still OK, but no change
        
        post = requests.get(f"{BASE_URL}/posts/{post_id}").json()
        assert post['likesCount'] == 1  # Count shouldn't change
        
        # Unlike the post
        unlike_response = requests.delete(f"{BASE_URL}/posts/{post_id}/like", headers=headers)
        assert unlike_response.status_code == 200
        
        post = requests.get(f"{BASE_URL}/posts/{post_id}").json()
        assert post['likesCount'] == 0
        
        # Unlike again (should be idempotent)
        unlike_response2 = requests.delete(f"{BASE_URL}/posts/{post_id}/like", headers=headers)
        assert unlike_response2.status_code == 200

    def test_comment_threading(self):
        """Test nested comments and threading"""
        headers = get_auth_headers("testuser")
        
        # Create parent post
        post_response = requests.post(f"{BASE_URL}/posts", headers=headers, json={
            "content": "Discussion thread test"
        })
        post_id = post_response.json()['id']
        
        # Add top-level comment
        comment1 = requests.post(f"{BASE_URL}/posts/{post_id}/comments", headers=headers, json={
            "content": "This is the first comment"
        }).json()
        comment1_id = comment1['id']
        
        # Reply to comment
        comment2 = requests.post(f"{BASE_URL}/comments/{comment1_id}/replies", headers=headers, json={
            "content": "This is a reply"
        }).json()
        
        # Get comment with replies
        comment = requests.get(f"{BASE_URL}/comments/{comment1_id}").json()
        assert comment['repliesCount'] == 1
        
        # Get all comments for post (should show threading)
        comments = requests.get(f"{BASE_URL}/posts/{post_id}/comments", params={"threaded": True}).json()
        assert len(comments) == 1  # Only top-level
        assert comments[0]['replies'][0]['id'] == comment2['id']

    def test_delete_post_cascade(self):
        """Test that deleting a post removes all associated interactions"""
        user1_headers = get_auth_headers("user1")
        user2_headers = get_auth_headers("user2")
        
        # User1 creates post
        post_response = requests.post(f"{BASE_URL}/posts", headers=user1_headers, json={
            "content": "This post will be deleted"
        })
        post_id = post_response.json()['id']
        
        # User2 likes and comments
        requests.post(f"{BASE_URL}/posts/{post_id}/like", headers=user2_headers)
        comment = requests.post(f"{BASE_URL}/posts/{post_id}/comments", headers=user2_headers, json={
            "content": "Nice post!"
        }).json()
        comment_id = comment['id']
        
        # User1 deletes post
        delete_response = requests.delete(f"{BASE_URL}/posts/{post_id}", headers=user1_headers)
        assert delete_response.status_code == 204
        
        # Verify post is gone
        get_response = requests.get(f"{BASE_URL}/posts/{post_id}")
        assert get_response.status_code == 404
        
        # Verify like is gone (by checking user2's liked posts)
        liked = requests.get(f"{BASE_URL}/users/user2/liked-posts", headers=user2_headers).json()
        assert post_id not in liked
        
        # Verify comment is gone
        comment_response = requests.get(f"{BASE_URL}/comments/{comment_id}")
        assert comment_response.status_code == 404

    def test_repost_functionality(self):
        """Test reposting with and without additional content"""
        headers = get_auth_headers("user1")
        
        # Create original post
        post_response = requests.post(f"{BASE_URL}/posts", headers=headers, json={
            "content": "Original viral content"
        })
        original_id = post_response.json()['id']
        
        # Simple repost (no additional content)
        repost_data = {
            "originalPostId": original_id,
            "type": "repost"
        }
        repost_response = requests.post(f"{BASE_URL}/posts", headers=get_auth_headers("user2"), json=repost_data)
        assert repost_response.status_code == 201
        repost = repost_response.json()
        assert repost['type'] == 'repost'
        assert repost['originalPost']['id'] == original_id
        
        # Quote repost (with additional content)
        quote_data = {
            "content": "This is so true! 👏",
            "originalPostId": original_id,
            "type": "quote"
        }
        quote_response = requests.post(f"{BASE_URL}/posts", headers=get_auth_headers("user3"), json=quote_data)
        assert quote_response.status_code == 201
        
        # Check original post's repost count
        original = requests.get(f"{BASE_URL}/posts/{original_id}").json()
        assert original['repostsCount'] == 2
